struct.name: CRS_POS
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Cursor position, CRS_0. The table gives 16-bit X in bits 15:0 and Y in bits 31:16, reset zero. The spec's functional text (pp. 20-22) calls positions 12-bit, and NetBSD treats the fields as signed. Width and signedness are unresolved.

struct.name: CTRLSTAT
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Pin pair n is data at bit 6+2n and an active-low output enable at bit 7+2n, for n = 0 to 9. Reset is 11 for every pair (data high, output disabled), so every pin is an input. Bit 4 is the monitor sense pin, an external read-only input whose polarity and wiring are not established. Bits 26 (half-phase) and 27 (composite sync polarity) reset to zero. Bits 3:0 are the chip revision, read-only.

struct.doc: Bits 22 (out of range) and 23 (out of lock) are status bits. The table leaves their reset contents unspecified, and the spec gives no PLL lock time or frequency limits. Bits 25:24 are manufacturer test controls and are not described.

struct.name: FP_HDRV
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The three flat-panel drive registers and the three start-preset registers share one layout: two 12-bit counts, "off" or "x" in the low half. The specification names them VT_10 to VT_12 and VT_17 to VT_19 (pages 39 and 40). It compares FP_HDRV, FP_DE and the "x" halves with the horizontal counter and FP_VDRV and the "y" halves with the vertical counter, but it compares both halves of FP_DE with the horizontal counter. The totals shipped software writes for two fixed panels (806 and 771, 1065 and 1024) look like line counts, not pixel counts (inferred from magnitude); which counter FP_DE really uses is unknown.

struct.name: I2C
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Monitor DDC bus. Bit 0 is the data line and bit 1 the clock line; both reset to 1. The spec gives separate output and synchronized input pins (page 22): a write sets the outputs, and a read returns the bus state, which can differ from the output latch. NetBSD XORs both written and read bits with 3 and calls the fields low active. That is a software expectation (inferred), and the register table alone does not say whether writing 1 releases a line. Whether the reset value 1 means released is therefore not established.

struct.name: I2CFP
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Flat-panel DDC bus, same layout as I2C: data at bit 0 and clock at bit 1, both reset to 1. The spec places external pullups on the flat-panel clock and data outputs (page 4). The inverted-convention caveat under I2C applies here too.

struct.name: VT_F2RF_LOCK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Field-to-frame lock line, VT_7. The page 21 diagram and the NetBSD encoding name a stereo toggle line and a frame-lock line. Which half holds which is inferred from the listing order in the register table, the same order the interrupt words use. No reset table is given.

struct.name: VT_FLAGS
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Output polarity and control bits 6:0 (VT_6). Composite sync low is bit 5. The other bits follow the public Linux and NetBSD encodings, which are software expectations, and the table gives no reset value for them.
